claims.text: Denrell showed in 2003 that the organisations we can observe are the survivors of a selective process that eliminated a large fraction of the underlying population.
claims.quote: The organizations that can be observed at any point in time are the survivors of a selective process that has eliminated a large fraction of the underlying population

claims.text: Risky practices unrelated to performance in the full population may seem positively related to performance in a sample of survivors.
claims.quote: risky practices, even if they are unrelated to performance in the full population of organizations, may seem to be positively related to performance in a sample of survivors.

claims.text: Record labels behave like investors: someone with capital chooses which artist to put it behind, and often the talent was the songs, the production and the access, not the performer.
claims.quote: Record labels behave like investors: someone with capital chooses which artist to put it behind.

claims.text: From 2010 to 2014 the top ten producers were behind about 40% of songs reaching the top five of the Billboard Hot 100, against about 19% in the late 1980s.
claims.quote: the top ten producers were behind about 40% of the songs

value.unit: percent of top-five songs by the top ten producers

claims.text: In one week of October 2015 only two songs on the Hot 100 were written by a single person, against 51 in 1975.
claims.quote: two songs on the Hot 100 were written by a single person

value.unit: Hot 100 songs written by one person

claims.text: After three members of TVXQ challenged a 13-year contract in 2009, Korea's fair trade watchdog set seven years as the maximum for standard contracts.
claims.quote: set seven years as the maximum

value.unit: years maximum for standard entertainer contracts

claims.text: When a venture capitalist on a startup's board dies unexpectedly, startups become more likely to fail; Ewens and Sosyura conclude a VC's network and reputation are key irreplaceable assets.
claims.quote: a VC's network and reputation are key irreplaceable assets.

claims.text: When an investor chooses between two founders with the same idea, drive and talent, one deciding factor is which founder the investor believes they can control.
claims.quote: My hypothesis is that one of the deciding factors is control

claims.text: Investors say it openly: Steve Krein of StartUp Health always asks whether an entrepreneur is coachable.
claims.quote: one thing he always looks for in an entrepreneur is the question "Are they coachable?"

claims.text: Reviewing the evidence in 2023, Letwin and colleagues wrote that investors prefer coachable entrepreneurs, but being coachable does not necessarily make a firm more successful.
claims.quote: While investors and support organizations such as accelerators prefer coachable entrepreneurs, being coachable doesn't necessarily make your firm more successful.

claims.text: If investors reliably select on a trait that does not predict success, something other than success is being selected for: coachability is a polite word, controllability a less polite one.
claims.quote: Coachability is a polite word for it. Controllability is a less polite one.

claims.text: Kaplan and Strömberg read 213 venture investments in 119 companies and found cash-flow, voting, board and liquidation rights allocated separately and contingent on performance.
claims.quote: 213 venture investments in 119 companies

claims.text: If the firm performs poorly the VCs obtain full control; as it improves the entrepreneur gains control; if it performs very well the VCs keep cash-flow rights but relinquish most control.
claims.quote: if the firm performs poorly, the VCs obtain full control.

claims.text: The big stick is the point at which the founder, or the artist, can credibly say I leave and you cannot replace me, and the contract hands power back.
claims.quote: once the founder, or the artist, can credibly say "I leave and you cannot replace me", the contract hands power back

claims.text: The same study found it common for VCs to include non-compete and vesting provisions that make it more expensive for the entrepreneur to leave; replaceability is designed in.
claims.quote: common for VCs to include non-compete and vesting provisions that make it more expensive for the entrepreneur to leave the firm

claims.text: In Wasserman's 2008 study of 212 US startups, 50% of founders were no longer CEO by year three and fewer than 25% led their companies' IPOs.
claims.quote: 50% of founders were no longer the CEO; in year four, only 40% were still in the corner office; and fewer than 25% led their companies' initial public offerings.

value.unit: percent of founders no longer CEO by year three

claims.text: The Ewens and Marx dataset of 11,929 venture-backed firms is more conservative: some 15% had at least one founder replacement in the sample period.
claims.quote: Some 15% of the 11,929 firms have at least one founder replacement in our sample period.

value.unit: percent of firms with a founder replacement

claims.text: In the MusicLab experiment, showing popularity made success more unequal and less predictable: the best songs rarely did poorly, the worst rarely did well, and any other result was possible.
claims.quote: The best songs rarely did poorly, and the worst rarely did well, but any other result was possible.

claims.text: Moretti found the ten largest clusters in computer science account for 69% of US inventors in the field, and inventors who move into a large cluster produce more.
claims.quote: the ten largest clusters in computer science account for 69% of US inventors

value.unit: percent of US computer science inventors in the ten largest clusters

claims.text: Wasserman's study of 6,130 US startups found each additional level of founder control reduces pre-money valuation by 17.1 to 22.0 percent.
claims.quote: reduces the pre-money valuation of the startup by 17.1-22.0 percent

value.unit: percent lower pre-money valuation per level of founder control, lower bound

claims.text: Ewens and Marx used changes in state non-compete laws to argue that replacing founders improves performance and makes a high-quality exit more likely.
claims.quote: to argue that replacing founders improves performance and makes a high-quality exit more likely

claims.text: Bain found that from 1990 to 2014 founder-led companies in the S&P 500 performed 3.1 times better in shareholder returns, and its 2026 update puts the gap since 2015 at 2.1 times.
claims.quote: founder-led companies in the S&P 500 "performed 3.1 times better" than the others in shareholder returns

claims.text: In April 2026 Mark Zuckerberg held 60.8% of Meta's voting power, and Page and Brin about 53% of Alphabet's, through shares with ten votes each.
claims.quote: in April 2026 Mark Zuckerberg held 60.8% of Meta's voting power

claims.text: There is a selection effect inside the investors' evidence: the strong-minded founders who walked away, bootstrapped or never got funded are mostly not in the sample.
claims.quote: The strong-minded founders who walked away, bootstrapped or never got funded are mostly not in the sample.

claims.text: The hypothesis can be tested in three ways: follow coachability ratings for ten years, compare the mission rather than the multiple, and count the founders who refused term sheets.
claims.quote: The hypothesis can be tested, and I would like to see it done.

claims.text: Survey founders who were offered term sheets and refused them; if the refusers score higher on independence and lower on coachability, the filter is real.
claims.quote: Survey founders who were offered term sheets and refused them, and compare them with those who signed.

claims.text: If the hypothesis holds, the founder with a strong vision, a clear direction and strong ethics is at a disadvantage in early-stage funding, because an investor reads them as hard to overrule.
claims.quote: If the hypothesis holds, a particular profile is at a disadvantage in early-stage funding

claims.text: The practical conclusion is to get to the big stick before you need investors' money, so that the choice of investor is yours; agents making execution cheap make that more possible.
claims.quote: It is to get to the big stick before you need their money, so that the choice of investor is yours.

claims.text: No study tests controllability directly; coachability is the nearest proxy, and the link between them is the owner's argument.
claims.quote: No study tests "controllability" directly.

claims.text: The value evidence cuts against the argument: Wasserman and Ewens and Marx find less founder control and founder replacement go with higher valuations and better exits.
claims.quote: The value evidence cuts against me.

claims.text: Bain's figures are its own analysis, not peer-reviewed, and founder-led includes founders who stayed on the board.
claims.quote: Bain's figures are its own analysis.

claims.text: The founder-tenure figures are old; Wasserman's sample covers startups from the late 1990s and early 2000s.
claims.quote: The founder-tenure figures are old.

claims.text: The music figures are mostly industry analyses, not peer-reviewed studies.
claims.quote: The music figures are mostly industry analyses

claims.text: The article does not claim investors are villains; their incentive is a return, and selecting for control follows from that.
claims.quote: Not that investors are villains.

claims.text: Nor that strong founders always win; some are hard to work with for reasons that have nothing to do with ethics, and the owner is a founder with a stake in the argument.
claims.quote: Not that strong founders always win.
